english: Dyeus, father, hear us, you who give us rain, who give (bring) us light. Earth, mother, listen to us, you who nourish the cattle, who carry the mountains. Give us good fame. Mother, give us rye and wool.
uncertain: pérwr̥h₂: NEUT.PL of 'ford, crossing' or 'rock, mountain'; 'mountains' chosen (earth bearing them)
nos: ACC/GEN/DAT enclitic; dative/object 'us' from context
dyéw: VOC (also LOC); vocative from address

english: Mother, we are ploughing your field. Be kind to us, and may the rye grow. May the seed and the apples grow. May the wolf not come to us. May the dog guard the sheep; may the cloud rain on the rye. Mother, let us give you mead.
uncertain: h₁uséwih₂: fem NOM/VOC.SG of 'good', predicate 'be good/kind (to us)'
dédeh₃omes: SBJV.1PL 'let us give / we shall give'
séh₁mn̥: singular 'seed', conjoined subject with plural optative

english: The Sun's daughter sank in the deep sea. The mother was searching for her own daughter. She said to Dawn: 'Dawn, did you see her?' Then Dawn said to her: 'I saw her. She sank over there.' Then the mother said to the twins: 'Twins, rescue her from the sea.' Then the twins heard her. Riding with horses, the two went to the sea. Then they seized the daughter and led her out of the sea. She was rescued. Then the mother rejoiced and gave the twins good fame.
uncertain: spr̥tóm: AOR.2DU or IMP.2DU; imperative in request
yemHóh₁: INS.SG or NOM/VOC/ACC.DU; vocative dual then nominative dual
h₂uséy: DAT.SG of 'dawn' (alt. LOC of h₂owsis / 'ear')

english: Who stretched out the heavy sky above? Who laid the earth below? Who let the waters go into the deep sea? Who made the swift light above? The great god stretched out the sky. And he laid her (earth) below. And he let them (the waters) go into the sea, and made the light. To which god shall we give mead? To him let us give mead.
uncertain: tn̥néwt: PST.3SG 'was stretching'; rendered as simple past
móri: ACC of goal 'into the sea'
tā́m: fem ACC.SG, refers to earth (dʰéǵʰōm is f)
téh₂: neut ACC.PL, refers to waters
déh₃omes/dédeh₃omes: SBJV.1PL 'shall we / let us give'

english: The priest (libation-pourer) said to the king: 'Sacrifice to (worship) the god Werunos.'
uncertain: ǵʰéwtōr: lexicon gloss only 'to pour'; agent noun 'pourer' = priest
wérunom: not in lexicon (near-miss); taken as proper name Werunos (cf. Varuna/Ouranos), ACC.SG
tom, wewked: unaccented / -d spelling, different orthography; wewked AOR.3SG 'said'

english: The sheep said to the horses: 'My heart pains me, seeing (that I see) a man driving horses.'
uncertain: h₁ékʷoybʰyos: lexicon gap; non-palatal ékʷ- spelling of 'horse' DAT.PL, inconsistent with h₁éḱwoms in same line
dʰǵʰémonm̥: lexicon gap; taken as 'man, earthling' ACC.SG
agʰnutor: lexicon gap; taken as middle 'is pained/grieves'
h₂áǵeti: a-colored spelling; PRS.3SG 'drives' (paratactic 'I see a man (he) drives')

english: Gods and goddesses, hear us, you who dwell in the sky, you who sit on the heights, you who go through the deep waters. We give you poured mead. Protect us; may our cattle be healthy. Give us swift horses.
uncertain: tḱité, sédyete, h₁ité: PRS/PST/IMP.2PL ambiguous; present in relative clauses
ǵʰutóm: 'poured, libated' NEUT.ACC.SG agreeing with médʰu (not AOR.2DU)

english: The brother's sister (or: the sister, to the brother) said: 'Who struck the serpent?' Then the brother said to her: 'The giver of rain struck the serpent.' She said: 'With what did he strike?' 'He struck with a stone and with thunder. Striking it, he released the waters.' Then she said: 'Did the serpent die?' 'It died, and the waters ran off to the sea.' Then she said: 'His name is famous.'
misfit: bʰréh₂tr̥s: GEN/ABL.SG where the addressee of 'said' should be DAT bʰréh₂trey (as elsewhere in the set); only reading is 'the brother's sister said'

english: Fire was with the gods. It was not with men. Then a man went to the mountain of the gods. Having seized the fire, he hid it in a heavy stone. Then he went down and sweated. Dyeus saw him and said to him: 'Give the fire back.' Then he said: 'I will not give it back.' Then he (Dyeus) struck him with thunder and split [him/the stone]. It (the fire) went away from them. And now they seek it in stone.
uncertain: tód tóns h₂ew gʷéh₂t: h₂ew 'away from' / 'back'; 'it went away from them' or 'back to them (gods)'
misfit: bʰindth₂é: MID.PST.2SG in a 3SG narrative clause (só-kʷe ...); expected 3SG bʰindtó

english: The rye dried up, and the cattle were thirsty and were sweating. Then the men were looking at the sky. They said: 'Where is the cloud?' Then a cloud came forth from the heights. The cloud rained. The streams filled and the rye grew. The apples were plump. Then they rejoiced.
uncertain: tr̥syónt/swidyónt/spéḱyont: PST.3PL (also PTCP forms); finite reading
sréwmn̥h₂ pléh₁t: neuter plural subject with 3SG verb (regular)

english: Dawn came forth from the darkness. She was red. She was the daughter of the sky (Dyeus). Then Dyeus saw her and rejoiced. Then her light went forth. The goose woke up, and she roused the cattle. The darkness vanished. Then he (Dyeus) gave (set) her a famous name.
uncertain: séh₂-kʷe gʷṓs woǵéyet: fem 'she' may be the goose (f) or Dawn

english: God of the rain-cloud, come to us. You are great; bring us rain. Slay the serpent who enclosed the waters. Do not leave us. Listen to my word; protect our sheep. May the wolf not eat them. May our cattle live. And may our rye be thriving. Then let us give you mead.
uncertain: mē nos linékʷs: mē + injunctive (PST.2SG form) = prohibitive
wékʷos moy: moy GEN 'my word' or DAT
tā́s: fem ACC.PL refers to sheep (h₂ówis f)
misfit: Hrugʰéys: GEN/ABL.SG used as subject of h₁syéh₁t with NOM predicate sph₁rós; expected NOM Hrugʰís

english: God of thunder, you who struck the serpent with a stone, who released the waters from the heights, who freed the cattle, who drive swift horses: the sea trembles at your feet. You give us heavy rain. Do not dry up our fields. Your imperishable fame lives. Now, giver of rain, hear us. Give us cattle and good fame.
misfit: dh₃té: IMP.2PL addressed to a single god (all other verbs 2SG: kélh₂s, sélǵs, h₂éǵesi, ḱludʰí); expected dh₃dʰí

english: The twin came to the Sun. He said: 'Sun, give me your daughter. I will give you ten cows and four horses.' Then the father said: 'Be my son-in-law.' Then the twin gave them, and the father gave him his own daughter. Then the two drank.
uncertain: sóh₂wl̥: ACC of goal 'to the sun', then VOC
moy/toy: DAT 'to me' / GEN 'your', and DAT 'to you'

english: The sister saw a god on the height, and she became afraid. She said to her own brother: 'Who is he?' Then the brother said to her: 'He is the giver of rain, and he strikes the serpent.' Then she said: 'Let us give him a horse.' Then the two gave him a horse.
uncertain: déh₃womes: SBJV.1PL 'let us' for two speakers (dual would be expected, but plural acceptable)

english: The god of thunder was driving swift horses. The thunder went, and the cloud followed him. His wheels turned. The serpent saw him. Then it trembled and crawled down (away). He slew the serpent. He released the waters. Then he went away.
Dawn, daughter of the sky, shine for us. You who drive away the darkness, who wake us again, who lead the cattle to the pasture, who redden again above: your light is good. Dawn, give us light.

Swift twins, come to us, you who rescued us from the sea, who drive swift horses, who draw the chariot, who tamed the horses. Twins, hear us; guard our horses. May our horses be healthy. Givers of good things, give us horses.
uncertain: gʷm̥tóm, ḱlutóm, ph₂stóm: IMP.2DU (homonymous with AOR/PST.2DU or adjectives)
spr̥tóm, dm̥h₂tóm: AOR.2DU in relative clauses ('rescued', 'tamed')

english: The son said to his father: 'Who holds up the sky?' Then the father said to him: 'The gods hold it up. Son, look up.' Then the son said: 'Who guards the gods?' 'Father Dyeus guards them.'

The sea swelled and the fire went out. Then the men grew cold and trembled. They said: 'Who will bring us fire?' Then the dog said: 'I will bring it to you.' Then the dog reached the height of the gods. Having seized the fire, the dog ran back. Then it brought it to them. They brought it meat. It ate that. And now it lives with them.
uncertain: tód tóns bʰéret: tóns ACC.PL as goal 'to them' (dative tóybʰos would be usual)

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled to the field (plain).
uncertain: tod, ḱeḱluwōs, owis, aǵrom, ebʰuget: unaccented, laryngeal-less orthography unlike the rest of the set
aǵrom: lexicon gap; = h₂éǵrom 'field', ACC of goal
ebʰuget: near-miss; augmented past of bʰewg- 'flee'
ḱeḱluwōs: masc PTCP.PRF with fem 'sheep' (fem ḱeḱluwúsih₂ would be expected), possible agreement slip

english: The Sun's daughter shone. Then the two sons of the sky arrived with horses. The Sun said to her: 'These two have come to love you.' Then she said: 'I will go with them.' Then he gave her to them. She clothed herself in a good garment, and she wore silver. The two placed her in a silver chariot and led her away. Then the gods drank mead and rejoiced. Then Dawn shone. She was red, and the Sun's chariot went forth.
uncertain: tóybʰos, tṓys: plural pronouns for the two sons (dual not used)

english: The serpent struck the god, and he lay down. Then the god's brother came. He said to him: 'Brother, stand up and strike the serpent.' Then he stood up and grew strong. The two struck the serpent, and it died. Then he released the waters. Their fame was great.
uncertain: tósmey wéwket: speaker/addressee unclear (brother addressing fallen god, who then stands up)
tóysōm: GEN.PL for two (dual not used)

english: Fire ran away from the gods and sank into the waters. Then the gods were searching for him. They did not find him. A goose was swimming. Then she saw him there and said to them: 'Fire is in the water.' Then they said: 'Fire, come out of the water.' Then Fire said: 'I am afraid.' Then Fire came out of it.

The serpent was great and heavy. It shut the waters in the rock, and the water did not flow forth. The rye dried up and the cattle were thirsty. Then the god of thunder came to it (the rock). He slew the serpent with a stone. He split it (the rock), and they (the waters) ran forth. Then he freed the cattle from it. The cattle were free. The thunder roared and the cloud rained. Then they gave him great fame. Then he rode away with his horses. The rye grew.
uncertain: tód: neuter, read as the rock (péruni) rather than the masc serpent
téh₂: neut NOM.PL = waters, with 3SG verb (regular)
misfit: h₁stā́m: 3DU 'the two were' with plural subject gʷówes h₁léwdʰerōs; expected 3PL h₁sént

english: If a man urinates in a river, the goddess shall strike him. Whoever urinates in a stream, the waters (?) shall push/strike him. Whoever puts filth into a spring, he shall go away from the field (be banished).
uncertain: h₂ékʷeh₂es: NOM.PL 'waters' (parallel to déywih₂ as subject) or GEN.SG 'in a stream of water' leaving stunédtu without an expressed subject
misfit: h₂ékʷeh₂es: NOM.PL (feminine) as subject of IMP.3SG stunédtu, where the parallel clauses (déywih₂ ... gʷʰn̥sḱétu; só ... léyttu) want NOM.SG h₂ékʷeh₂; feminine plural cannot take a singular verb. Unless read as GEN.SG 'stream of water', which leaves stunédtu without a subject

english: The gods arranged the sky and the earth. The sun walks its own path. Dawn comes, and it (the sun) follows her. The water goes to the deep sea. The cattle go to the pasture. The cloud has rained, and the waters fill the rivers. The apples ripen. Now let us go on that path.
uncertain: swóh₁ stóygʰoh₁ / tóh₁ stóygʰoh₁: INS.SG 'by (its own/that) path' or ACC.DU 'two paths'
tód: neut = the sun (sóh₂wl̥ n); tā́m = Dawn

english: The sky (Dyeus) lay on the earth, and he was heavy, and darkness was there. Then the great god split sky and earth apart. He lifted it (the sky) up and set it above. He laid the earth below. Then light came forth and the darkness went away. The earth was broad and the sky was great.
